definition: Shady or thickly overshadowed; also, less commonly, prone to take offense.
etymology: It grew from Latin umbrosus, “full of shade,” itself from umbra, “shadow.” English first used it for sheltering foliage and deep shade; its touchy sense followed the separate noun umbrage, meaning offense or displeasure.
usage: By late October, the wood was no longer umbrageous: each thinning bough admitted another pale piece of sky.
